Childhood 
A variety of nutritional inadequacies exist among school-aged children (aged 5–12 years), ranging from overeating 
(caloric excess) to undereating, often due to food insecurity. Children who overeat or undereat are at risk for 
hematologic consequences from nutritional deficiencies. Iron deficiency is the most common micronutrient 
deficiency in school-aged children, although this age group has the lowest prevalence overall among all children.
